title: Colgate-Palmolive India Hands Palmolive's D2C Business to Bombay Shaving Company
excerpt: The FMCG giant taps its portfolio company's digital-first expertise to revive Palmolive's underperforming online and direct-to-consumer operations.
body:
• Colgate-Palmolive India has transferred Palmolive's direct-to-consumer and e-commerce operations to Bombay Shaving Company (BSC), a grooming startup on its cap table since 2018.
  • Colgate MD Prabha Narasimhan acknowledged the company "failed miserably" with Palmolive's digital play at the Analyst Meet 2026, prompting the handover.
  • BSC will manage end-to-end D2C and online sales for Palmolive, while Colgate retains control of product development, supply chain, and offline trade.
  • E-commerce already contributes over 10% of Colgate India's revenue with margins roughly 400 basis points higher than traditional channels.

Colgate Admits Palmolive's Digital Failure

Colgate-Palmolive India has handed over the direct-to-consumer and e-commerce operations for its Palmolive personal care brand to Bombay Shaving Company, the Delhi NCR-based grooming startup in which it has held a minority stake since 2018. The move signals a strategic reset for a legacy brand that has struggled to gain traction in India's fast-growing online marketplace.

Colgate-Palmolive India Managing Director and CEO Prabha Narasimhan was blunt about the brand's shortcomings during the company's Analyst Meet 2026. "When it comes to Palmolive, the company has failed miserably," she said, referring to the personal care label's inability to break through in digital channels despite the parent company's broader e-commerce momentum.

"When it comes to Palmolive, the company has failed miserably."

— Prabha Narasimhan, MD & CEO, Colgate-Palmolive India

How the Partnership Works

Under the new arrangement, Bombay Shaving Company takes charge of Palmolive's D2C website and e-commerce customer connections, running advertising-to-consumer operations end to end. Colgate retains ownership of the Palmolive brand's product pipeline, supply chain, quality standards, and innovation, as well as all modern trade, general trade, and above-the-line advertising.

Jacob Madukkakuzhy, Whole-time Director and CFO of Colgate-Palmolive India, clarified during the analyst Q&A that Bombay Shaving Company's mandate is strictly limited to direct-to-consumer and online sales. "The end-to-end mission of Bombay Shaving Company only applies to D2C and online," he said. Colgate will still manage conventional and modern trade channels independently.

The deal extends beyond a consulting arrangement. BSC will operationally manage customer acquisition, digital marketing, and the online purchase funnel — areas where the startup has built domain expertise since its founding in 2016 by former McKinsey consultant Shantanu Deshpande.

The E-Commerce Opportunity

The strategic pivot is informed by hard numbers. Colgate-Palmolive India now directs nearly 60% of its advertising budget to digital channels, with the remaining 40% going to television. E-commerce contributes more than 10% of the company's revenue, growing at double-digit rates with margins approximately 400 basis points above the company average. Over half of Colgate's online sales are premium products, and its e-commerce market share runs roughly 400 basis points ahead of its overall market position.

Management cited the emergence of quick commerce as an additional accelerant. Platforms like Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart have expanded the addressable market for personal care products online, creating a channel that rewards brands with strong digital execution — precisely the capability Colgate has found difficult to build internally for Palmolive.

BSC's Digital Track Record

Bombay Shaving Company, which now operates over 100 SKUs across shaving, grooming, skincare, and a women's hair-removal line called Bombae, has built its business on a digital-first, omnichannel model combining D2C, quick commerce, and retail distribution. The company has reported a net revenue run-rate exceeding ₹550 crore and has reached PAT profitability, according to its most recent disclosures.

Colgate-Palmolive Asia Pacific first invested approximately ₹18 crore for a 14% stake in BSC's Series A in 2018. Reckitt Benckiser later joined the cap table with a ₹45 crore round in 2021, followed by a ₹210 crore Series C led by Malabar Investments in 2022. The company has been raising funds toward an eventual public listing.

"E-commerce has several positive effects on growth, margin, premiumisation, and share, and rapid commerce only serves to amplify these trends."

— Prabha Narasimhan, MD & CEO, Colgate-Palmolive India

What to Watch

If the arrangement delivers, it could serve as a template for other legacy FMCG companies seeking to turbocharge their online presence without building D2C capabilities from scratch. For Bombay Shaving Company, the operational responsibility adds a marquee brand to its portfolio while demonstrating the scalability of its digital playbook beyond its own labels. The question is whether the startup's digital DNA can translate to a brand with fundamentally different positioning in a category — personal care — where Palmolive competes against entrenched players like Hindustan Unilever and ITC.
nri_angle: Colgate-Palmolive India's partnership with Bombay Shaving Company reflects evolving digital strategies in India's consumer goods market.
